mainTopic: Whether the טומאה of liquids is from the Torah or from the רבנן: the ברייתא of רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר, the רב/שמואל dispute about the מקדש liquids, and the verses about liquids and הכשר
overview: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with three positions on a ספק about the טומאה of liquids (משקין). רבי מאיר, joined by רבי אלעזר, says a doubtful liquid is itself טמא but does not make others טמא. רבי יהודה says it is טמא for everything. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say it makes foods טמא but not vessels. The key idea is that a doubt in a Torah law is treated strictly and a doubt in a rabbinic law leniently. The גמרא then asks how רבי אלעזר can agree with רבי מאיר, since elsewhere he says liquids have no טומאה at all, based on יוסי בן יועזר's testimony that the liquids of the מקדש slaughterhouse are pure. This fits שמואל's reading of that testimony, and רב נחמן בר יצחק tries to answer for רב, but the wording of the ברייתא leaves רב with a קשיא. The גמרא then explains רב (all liquid טומאה is rabbinic) and שמואל (a liquid's own טומאה is from the Torah, and making others טמא is rabbinic). A verse is raised against שמואל, and it too ends in a קשיא. Finally, the גמרא tests whether liquid טומאה is from the Torah using verses about drinks, הכשר, and springs. It then begins explaining that only the blood of קדשים fails to cause הכשר, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר on doubtful liquids
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that according to רבי מאיר, a liquid in doubt is itself טמא but does not make other things טמא. רבי אלעזר agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is a doubt whether a liquid became impure, it is impure. If the doubt is about whether it made other things impure, they are pure. These are the words of רבי מאיר, and רבי אלעזר used to say the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that opens a מחלוקת about doubts involving the טומאה of liquids. The first view is that of רבי מאיר, and רבי אלעזר agrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of thumb is simple: a doubt in a Torah law is treated strictly, and a doubt in a rabbinic law is treated leniently. רבי מאיר is strict about the liquid itself becoming טמא, which shows he holds that part is דאורייתא. He is lenient about the liquid passing טומאה to other things, which shows he holds that part is only דרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with his words; agreeing with him

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up לִיטָּמֵא (the liquid itself becoming impure) with לְטַמֵּא (the liquid making something else impure). The entire מחלוקת turns on this difference.
steps.whyThisMatters: The line saying רבי אלעזר agrees with רבי מאיר is what the גמרא will challenge below.

phrases.english: A doubt whether liquids became impure: impure.
phrases.notes: The liquid itself is treated strictly.

phrases.english: A doubt about making others impure: pure,
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר כִּדְבָרָיו.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar would likewise say as his words.
phrases.notes: This is the line that gets challenged later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf about whether the טומאה of liquids is from the Torah, by bringing this ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר, a doubtful liquid is itself טמא but does not make others טמא.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: impure in every case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that a doubtful liquid is טמא in every respect, including making other things טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: it is impure for everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second, stricter view. רבי יהודה treats every doubt here strictly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהודה is strict even about a liquid passing טומאה to others, he must hold that this too is דאורייתא. So for him, all liquid טומאה comes from the Torah.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: impure for everything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, opposing view within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a doubtful liquid is טמא and makes others טמא.

steps.title: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון: foods versus vessels
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון draw a line between two cases. A doubtful liquid makes foods טמא, but vessels stay טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: regarding foods, they are impure; regarding vessels, they are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third, middle view. This view splits the case by what the liquid touched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquids making food טמא is treated strictly, so these תנאים hold it is דאורייתא. Liquids making vessels טמא is treated leniently, so they hold it is only דרבנן.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three positions. רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר: the liquid itself becomes טמא from the Torah, but it does not pass טומאה to others. רבי יהודה: everything is from the Torah. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון: food is affected from the Torah, vessels only rabbinically.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
Regarding foods, impure; regarding vessels, pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final, middle view in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubtful liquid makes foods טמא, but not vessels.

steps.title: Does רבי אלעזר hold liquids have any impurity at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבי אלעזר agrees with רבי מאיר. Another ברייתא has רבי אלעזר saying liquids have no טומאה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי אלעזר really hold that liquids have any impurity at all? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי אלעזר says: liquids have no impurity at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the line from Step 1 by quoting a contradicting statement of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds the liquid itself becomes טמא by Torah law. The other ברייתא has רבי אלעזר saying liquids have no Torah טומאה at all. So how can רבי אלעזר be said to agree with רבי מאיר?

keyTerms.meaning: And does he really hold? (a challenging question)

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Elazar hold:
that liquids have any impurity in the world?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question that works as a challenge.

phrases.english: But it was taught: Rabbi Elazar says:
There is no impurity for liquids at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מַשְׁקִין אִית לְהוּ טוּמְאָה בָּעוֹלָם? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the attribution in Step 1 that רבי אלעזר agrees with רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement וכן היה רבי אלעזר אומר כדבריו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A contradiction between two sources. One has רבי אלעזר agreeing that liquids can become טמא by Torah law. The other has him denying any Torah טומאה for liquids.

steps.title: Proof from the testimony of יוסי בן יועזר
steps.stepSummary: Within the same ברייתא, רבי אלעזר proves his view from יוסי בן יועזר. He testified that the איל קמצא locust is kosher and that the liquids of the מקדש slaughterhouse are pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that this is so: יוסי בן יועזר of צרידה testified that the איל קמצא locust is kosher, and that the liquids of the slaughterhouse in the מקדש are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר backs up his claim that liquids have no Torah טומאה. His proof is a famous testimony about the liquids in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbinic decree of טומאה for liquids did not apply in the מקדש. So if the liquids there are pure, liquid טומאה must be only rabbinic and not from the Torah at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Know that it is so (introduces a proof)

steps.confusionAlert: The word דְּכַן appears twice with two meanings. For the locust it means kosher to eat. For the liquids it means טהור (pure).
steps.whyThisMatters: The exact meaning of דכן for the liquids is disputed by רב and שמואל. The rest of the סוגיא depends on that dispute.

phrases.aramaic: תֵּדַע, שֶׁהֲרֵי הֵעִיד (יוֹסֵף) בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה
phrases.english: Know that this is so, for Yosei ben Yo'ezer of Tzereida testified
about the eil kamtza locust that it is kosher,
and about the liquids of the slaughterhouse that they are pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the contradicting ברייתא with רבי אלעזר's own proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's claim that liquids have no Torah טומאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The testimony of יוסי בן יועזר that the liquids of the מקדש slaughterhouse are pure

steps.title: No problem according to שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction goes away according to שמואל. He reads דכן as meaning only that these liquids do not make others טמא, while they themselves can still become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to שמואל, who said pure means they do not make others impure, but they can become impure themselves. That fits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the contradiction can be solved according to one reading of the testimony. It is also setting up the real problem, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the testimony only shows that passing טומאה to others is rabbinic. Under that reading, when רבי אלעזר says there is no טומאה for liquids, he means no Torah power to make others טמא. That is exactly רבי מאיר's view, so the two sources fit together.

phrases.english: This works well according to Shmuel,
who said: pure from making others impure,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל טוּמְאַת עַצְמָן יֵשׁ לָהֶן — שַׁפִּיר.
phrases.english: but they do have their own impurity: it fits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the contradiction from Steps 4 and 5 is solved according to שמואל's reading of דכן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of a term (reading דכן as limited)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר denies all Torah טומאה for liquids.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to שמואל, רבי אלעזר only denies that liquids pass טומאה to others by Torah law, which matches רבי מאיר.

steps.title: But according to רב, what can be said?
steps.stepSummary: According to רב, דכן means the liquids are completely pure, even in themselves. So the contradiction with רבי מאיר comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב, who said pure means truly pure, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses the challenge according to רב's reading and asks what answer can be given. The next step offers an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If דכן means the liquids cannot become טמא at all, then רבי אלעזר denies even the liquid's own Torah טומאה. But רבי מאיר holds that a liquid itself does become טמא by Torah law. So how can רבי אלעזר agree with him? The next step gives an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: What can be said? (the difficulty stands for now)

steps.whatToRemember: The whole difficulty depends on how רב and שמואל read דכן. For שמואל the sources fit. For רב, רבי אלעזר seems to deny the very Torah טומאה that רבי מאיר accepts.

phrases.english: But according to Rav, who said: actually pure,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַב, דְּאָמַר דְּכַן מַמָּשׁ — מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the solution from Step 6 does not work for רב, so the challenge comes back.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 1 that רבי אלעזר agrees with רבי מאיר, according to רב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רב, the testimony means liquids cannot become טמא at all. Then רבי אלעזר denies the liquid's own Torah טומאה, which contradicts רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר agrees with רבי מאיר on only one point
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the contradiction for רב. When the ברייתא says רבי אלעזר agrees with רבי מאיר, it means on only one of רבי מאיר's two rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: He agrees with him on one point.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק tries to save רב's view. He says רבי אלעזר agrees with רבי מאיר only partly, not completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר gave two rulings about a doubtful liquid. It becomes טמא itself, but it does not make other things טמא. רבי אלעזר agrees with the second half (it does not make others טמא), but he disagrees with the first half, because he holds liquids have no טומאה at all. So there is no contradiction with רב's reading of דכן.

keyTerms.meaning: On one point (agreement on only one of the rulings)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
On one (point).
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר agrees only that a doubtful liquid does not make others טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אַחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7 against רב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רבי אלעזר agrees with all of רבי מאיר's rulings, which would mean liquids can become טמא themselves.
steps.terutzMaskana: He agrees only that a doubtful liquid does not make others טמא, so he can still hold that liquids have no טומאה at all.

steps.title: The wording of the ברייתא shows full agreement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back using two words from the ברייתא. כדבריו ("like his words," plural) and וכן ("and likewise") both show complete agreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it says "like his words," meaning many of them! And furthermore, it teaches "and likewise"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer using the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural word כדבריו means רבי אלעזר agreed with more than one of רבי מאיר's points. The word וכן also suggests a full match. Both words go against the idea that he agreed on only one point.

keyTerms.meaning: Like his words (plural, so more than one point)

phrases.english: But it says "like his words," which are many.
And furthermore, it teaches "and likewise"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 8 based on the wording of the text.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that the agreement covers only one point
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's own words (a plural noun and "likewise") show the agreement was complete, not partial.

steps.title: The difficulty stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends this exchange with the word קשיא. The question against רב is left without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no good answer, and it closes this back-and-forth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קשיא means the challenge stands. It does not mean רב's view is fully rejected. Because of that, the ברייתא remains hard to explain according to רב, but שמואל's reading has no such problem.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult (an unanswered challenge, weaker than a full refutation)

steps.confusionAlert: קשיא is not the same as תיובתא. With קשיא the question stays open, but רב's view is not declared refuted.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא fits שמואל's reading of דכן easily. According to רב, it remains a קשיא.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 9 without a resolution.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Against רב, the contradiction from the ברייתא remains unanswered.

steps.title: Returning to the main dispute between רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: Under the heading גופא, the גמרא quotes the רב/שמואל dispute again so that it can explain it. רב says the liquids are truly pure. שמואל says they cannot make other things טמא, but they can become טמא themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רב said: "pure" means truly pure. And שמואל said: "pure" means they do not make others impure, but they can become impure themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the original statement of רב and שמואל. It is setting up the next steps, which explain the reasoning behind each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new argument. It is a deliberate restatement, which גופא signals, so that the גמרא can now explore the source of the dispute. The goal is to find what legal principle each אמורא holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself (returning to analyze a quoted statement)
Pure (the word in יוסי בן יועזר's testimony)
Impurity of others (making other things טמא)

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav said: "Pure" — actually pure.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: דְּכַן מִלְּטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת אֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: "Pure" in that they do not transmit impurity to others,
but they themselves can become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא discussion and returns to analyze the רב/שמואל dispute itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב says the liquids of the מקדש slaughterhouse are fully pure. שמואל says they cannot make others טמא, but they can become טמא themselves.

steps.title: רב's reasoning: all impurity of liquids is from the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that all impurity of liquids is a rabbinic decree. The רבנן made the decree only for ordinary liquids, not for the liquids of the מקדש slaughterhouse. So those liquids are fully pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said they are truly pure. He holds that the impurity of liquids is only from the רבנן, and when the רבנן made their decree, it was for ordinary liquids. For the liquids of the slaughterhouse, they made no decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב reads דכן as completely pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If liquid impurity were from the Torah, the רבנן could not exempt any liquid from it. Since רב holds the whole category is rabbinic, the רבנן were free to leave the מקדש liquids out of their decree completely. So these liquids neither become טמא nor make others טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: From the רבנן (a rabbinic decree, not from the Torah)

phrases.english: Rav said "pure" — actually pure,
he holds the impurity of liquids is rabbinic,
and when the Sages decreed — it was on ordinary liquids,
but on the liquids of the slaughterhouse — they did not decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר דְּכַן מַמָּשׁ, קָסָבַר טוּמְאַת מַשְׁקִין דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side (רב) of the dispute quoted in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All impurity of liquids is rabbinic. The decree never included the liquids of the מקדש slaughterhouse, so they are completely pure.

steps.title: שמואל's reasoning: two levels of liquid impurity
steps.stepSummary: שמואל holds that liquids becoming טמא themselves is from the Torah, but liquids making others טמא is only from the רבנן. The רבנן did not apply their decree to the slaughterhouse liquids, so those liquids do not make others טמא. Their own Torah-level impurity still remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said "pure" means they do not make others impure, but they can become impure themselves. He holds that the liquids' own impurity is from the Torah, but making others impure is only from the רבנן. When the רבנן decreed, it was for ordinary liquids, and for the slaughterhouse liquids they did not decree. And where they did not decree, that refers only to making others impure. The liquids' own impurity still applies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שמואל gives only partial purity to the מקדש liquids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל splits liquid impurity into two levels. The Torah level is the liquid itself becoming טמא, and the רבנן cannot cancel that. The rabbinic level is the liquid passing טומאה to other things, and only that level was left out for the slaughterhouse.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: all liquid impurity is rabbinic, so the מקדש liquids are fully pure. שמואל: a liquid's own impurity is from the Torah, and only making others טמא is rabbinic. So the מקדש liquids can still become טמא, but they do not make others טמא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the argument over the one word דכן really comes from a basic question: is the impurity of liquids from the Torah or from the רבנן?

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: דְּכַן מִלְּטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת אֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: "Pure" in that they do not transmit impurity to others,
but they themselves can become impure.
He holds the impurity of liquids themselves is by Torah law,
(while) to transmit impurity to others is rabbinic,
and when the Sages decreed — it was on ordinary liquids,
on the liquids of the slaughterhouse — they did not decree.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי לָא גְּזוּר רַבָּנַן — לְטַמּוֹיֵי אֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: And when the Sages did not decree — it was regarding transmitting impurity to others,
but they themselves can still become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: דְּכַן מִלְּטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second side (שמואל) of the dispute, in parallel to רב in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A liquid's own impurity is from the Torah, and making others טמא is rabbinic. The slaughterhouse exemption covers only the rabbinic level.

steps.title: A verse challenges שמואל: anything impure should pass on impurity
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא tells his son to ask רב פפא a question. How can שמואל say liquids become טמא themselves but do not make others טמא? The Torah says that anything טמא passes on impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חיננא said to his son: When you go in before רב פפא, raise this difficulty with him. Did שמואל really say the liquids are pure in the sense that they cannot make others impure, but they can become impure themselves? Read here the verse: 'And the flesh that touches anything impure shall not be eaten.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's position from Step 13. It asks how something can be טמא from the Torah and still not pass on impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says that meat touching 'anything טמא' becomes forbidden. That means anything that is טמא from the Torah also makes other things טמא from the Torah. שמואל tried to split these two things apart (self-impurity from the Torah, passing on impurity only from the רבנן). The verse seems to say they cannot be split.

keyTerms.meaning: Raise a contradiction against him (literally 'throw at him')

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא לִבְרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chinnana said to his son:
When you go in before Rav Pappa,
raise this contradiction to him:
Did Shmuel really say that they are pure
in the sense of not making others impure,
but they do have impurity of their own?
Read here:
'And the flesh that touches anything impure
shall not be eaten.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's explanation given in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that liquids are טמא themselves from the Torah but do not make others טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse shows that anything טמא from the Torah passes impurity on to what it touches. So self-impurity without passing it on should be impossible.

steps.title: Defending שמואל: like the fourth level in holy food
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא answers that we already know of a case where something is impure but does not pass impurity on: רביעי בקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי said: It is just like the fourth degree of impurity in holy food.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא defends שמואל. He points to an accepted case where something becomes unfit but does not pass that status on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קודש, impurity can reach a fourth level (רביעי), but that fourth level does not create a fifth. So there is a precedent for something that is affected itself without affecting others. The liquids could work the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like (a comparison to a known case)
The fourth degree of impurity in holy food, which goes no further

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
It is just like the fourth degree in holy food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a parallel accepted case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything affected by impurity must pass it on.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like רביעי בקודש, the liquids can be affected without passing the impurity on.

steps.title: רב אשי rejects the comparison
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the comparison does not work. רביעי בקודש is never called 'טמא', but these liquids are called 'טמא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: The fourth degree in holy food is not called 'impure.' This liquid is called 'impure'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי knocks down רב שישא's defense. He shows that the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רביעי בקודש is only 'פסול' (disqualified). It is not truly 'טמא', so it makes sense that it does not pass anything on. The liquids are called real 'טמא', so the verse 'touches anything טמא' does apply to them.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objected to it:
The fourth degree in holy food is not called 'impure,'
but this (the liquid) is called 'impure'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the liquids and רביעי בקודש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רביעי בקודש is only פסול, not טמא. The liquids are truly called טמא, so the verse about touching 'anything טמא' applies to them.

steps.title: The question on שמואל stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with קשיא. The challenge against שמואל has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this exchange. The question against שמואל is left without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רב שישא's comparison falls, nothing else defends שמואל's split between self-impurity and passing impurity on. The verse from Step 14 stands as an unresolved problem for his view.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's middle position (liquids become טמא themselves from the Torah but do not pass it on) is left with an unanswered קשיא. This is because anything truly called טמא should pass on impurity.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the cycle that began in Step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge to שמואל from the verse 'והבשר אשר יגע בכל טמא' remains unresolved.

steps.title: A verse seems to show liquids become impure from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the verse 'וכל משקה... יטמא'. It seems to say outright that liquids become טמא from the Torah, which goes against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And all drink that may be drunk in any vessel shall be impure'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new attempt to decide whether the impurity of liquids comes from the Torah. It brings a verse that seems to prove it does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said all impurity of liquids is only a rabbinic decree (Step 12). This verse appears to say directly that a drink in a vessel 'shall be טמא'. That would make the impurity of liquids Torah law.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'And all drink that may be drunk
in any vessel shall be impure'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line testing רב's view from Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That liquids become טמא from the Torah (against רב).
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא יא:לד, 'וכל משקה אשר ישתה בכל כלי יטמא'

steps.title: Rereading the verse: 'shall be impure' means making food susceptible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'יטמא' in this verse does not mean the liquid itself becomes טמא. It means the liquid makes food ready to receive impurity (הכשר).
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'shall be impure' mean? It means 'makes susceptible.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. It reads the verse in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become טמא after it has been wet by a liquid. That wetting is called הכשר. According to this reading, the verse teaches that drinks cause הכשר, not that drinks themselves become טמא. So רב survives.

keyTerms.meaning: Making food susceptible to impurity by wetting it

steps.confusionAlert: הכשר does not mean 'kosher' here! It means that a liquid has wet the food, which makes the food able to become טמא.

phrases.english: What is 'shall be impure'? It means making susceptible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The meaning of the word יטמא in the verse.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'יטמא' means the liquid itself becomes טמא. It could instead mean the liquid causes הכשר.

steps.title: But הכשר is already taught at the start of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the end of the verse would teach הכשר. The beginning of the same verse already teaches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Making susceptible? You already learn that from the beginning of the verse: 'From all food that may be eaten, on which water comes, shall be impure'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from Step 19. It says that reading would make the end of the verse repeat what the beginning already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the verse already says that food touched by water can become טמא, which is the law of הכשר. If the second half also just means הכשר, it is extra. That suggests the second half must mean something else, such as the liquid itself becoming טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: From the beginning of the verse

phrases.english: Making susceptible? You already learn that from the beginning of the verse,
'From all food that may be eaten,' etc.!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in Step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse should not say the same thing twice. Since הכשר is already in the first half, the second half must teach something new.

steps.title: One half is for detached water, one for attached water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both halves are needed. One teaches הכשר from water already detached (in vessels), and the other teaches הכשר from water still attached to the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is about detached water, and one is about attached water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the הכשר reading. It shows that each half of the verse teaches a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half mentions 'בכל כלי' (in any vessel), so it covers water that has already been taken from its source. The first half covers water still connected to the ground. Since the verse is no longer repetitive, the proof against רב falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Attached (water still connected to the ground)

steps.whatToRemember: The verse 'וכל משקה... יטמא' does not prove that liquids are טמא from the Torah. It can be read as teaching הכשר from detached water, while the first half teaches הכשר from attached water.

phrases.english: One is about detached water, and one is about attached water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the verse into two different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both halves of the verse teach the same law of הכשר, so one of them is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second half teaches הכשר from detached water in vessels, and the first half teaches הכשר from water attached to the ground.

steps.title: Why both detached and attached water had to be taught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the פסוק needed to teach הכשר for both תלושין and מחוברין. Each one has its own reason to matter, so neither can be learned from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If the Torah only taught detached water, we would say it causes הכשר because the person valued it by drawing it. Attached water would not. If the Torah only taught attached water, we would say it causes הכשר because it sits in its natural place and is important. Detached water would not. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from the last step. It shows that each half of the פסוק teaches something we could not have guessed from the other half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Detached water has one special feature: a person drew it, which shows he cares about it (אחשבינהו). Attached water has a different special feature: it stays in its natural spot (קיימי בדוכתייהו). Since each case has its own reason, learning one would not prove the other. That is why the Torah wrote both.

keyTerms.meaning: Detached water, taken from its source (for example, in vessels)
Water still attached to the ground or its source
He gave them importance (by drawing them)
They stand in their natural place

steps.whatToRemember: Both halves of the פסוק are needed. Detached water matters because a person valued it. Attached water matters because it sits in its natural place.

phrases.english: And both are necessary,
for if it had taught us only about detached water,
that would be because he gave it importance,
phrases.notes: He drew the water, which shows he values it.

phrases.english: but attached water, I would say not.
And if it had taught only attached water,
that would be because they stand in their place and are significant,
but detached water, I would say not;
so both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands step 21's answer into a full צריכותא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case has its own unique reason, so both must be written
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One case could have been learned from the other, so one half of the פסוק would be extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each case has a unique reason (being valued vs. sitting in place), so both halves are needed.

steps.title: Proof from 'a spring or cistern shall be pure'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new פסוק. It seems to show that liquids normally can become טמא, except a spring or a cistern.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'But a spring or a cistern, a gathering of water, shall be pure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another proof against רב. It tries to show that liquids become טמא from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says only a spring or a cistern 'shall be pure.' The suggestion is that other water, such as water in a vessel, can become טמא. If so, liquids become טמא מדאורייתא, which goes against רב.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"But a spring or a cistern,
a gathering of water, shall be pure."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main question from step 18 (are liquids טמא מדאורייתא?) with a new פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That liquids become טמא from the Torah, against רב
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא יא:לו, 'אך מעין ובור מקוה מים יהיה טהור', which implies other water can become טמא

steps.title: 'Shall be pure' means the person who immerses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. 'יהיה טהור' means a person who immerses in this water becomes pure from his own טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'shall be pure' mean? It means one becomes pure from his impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from the last step. It reads the פסוק differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that 'shall be pure' describes the water itself. The גמרא says it describes the person who immerses: he becomes pure. So the פסוק is about טבילה, not about whether liquids can become טמא. The proof against רב falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: From his impurity (the one who immerses)

steps.confusionAlert: 'טהור' here does not mean 'the water stays pure.' It means 'the person immersing becomes pure.'

phrases.english: What does "shall be pure" mean?
From his impurity.
phrases.notes: The one who immerses in it becomes pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully removes the proof from this פסוק
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof misread 'יהיה טהור' as describing the water. It actually describes the person who immerses becoming pure.

steps.title: Does detached water really cause הכשר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim from step 21 that detached water makes food ready for טומאה. It cites רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: the liquids of the מקדש slaughterhouse are pure and also do not cause הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does detached water cause הכשר? But רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: the liquids of the slaughterhouse are not only pure, they also do not make food ready for טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to step 21, which said detached water causes הכשר from the Torah. It now questions that claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The liquids of the מקדש slaughterhouse are detached liquids. Yet רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says they do not cause הכשר. If detached water caused הכשר מדאורייתא, it would be hard to say these liquids do not. This suggests that הכשר from detached water may only be מדרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: They make food ready to receive טומאה
The liquids of the slaughterhouse in the מקדש
It is not enough that they are...

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge opens the next part of the סוגיא. The גמרא will need to explain how the slaughterhouse liquids fit with detached water causing הכשר.

phrases.english: And does detached water make food susceptible?
But didn't Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina say:
the liquids of the slaughterhouse (in the Temple),
not only are they pure,
but they also do not make food susceptible.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְלוּשִׁין מִי מַכְשִׁירִין? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the claim in steps 21-22 that detached water causes הכשר, and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (steps 21-22) that detached water causes הכשר from the Torah
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the slaughterhouse liquids, which are detached, do not cause הכשר. This suggests detached water does not cause הכשר מדאורייתא.

steps.title: The statement was only about blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule about the slaughterhouse liquids was only talking about blood, not water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Explain that statement as referring to blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 25. It says רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא meant only the blood in the מקדש slaughterhouse, not every liquid there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge worked only if 'liquids' included water. By limiting the statement to blood, the גמרא removes the contradiction. Water that is already detached can still cause הכשר, as step 21 said. Only the blood of the slaughterhouse is the special exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Explain it / interpret it as (referring to)
Making food ready (able) to become טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying blood is not a liquid. Blood is one of the liquids that can cause הכשר. The point is only that this specific blood, of קדשים, is an exception.

phrases.english: Explain it as referring to blood,
phrases.notes: This limits רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement about the 'liquids of the slaughterhouse' to blood only.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25 by narrowing the scope of the source that was quoted against step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the challenging source (it was talking about blood only)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement covered all liquids of the slaughterhouse, including water, so detached water would not cause הכשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: His statement covers only the blood of קדשים. Detached water still causes הכשר.

steps.title: A source that blood of offerings does not cause הכשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer with רבי יוחנן's teaching from the פסוק 'על הארץ תשפכנו כמים': only blood that is poured out like water causes הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: From where do we know that the blood of קדשים does not cause הכשר? Because the פסוק says, 'You shall pour it on the ground like water.' Blood that is poured out like water causes הכשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show that blood of קדשים really is different and does not cause הכשר. This backs up the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares blood to water: 'pour it on the ground like water.' רבי יוחנן learns that blood poured out like water, such as the blood of an ordinary animal that spills on the ground, counts like water and causes הכשר. The other side of this teaching, that blood not poured like water (the blood of קרבנות, which is collected in a vessel) does not cause הכשר, comes right on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Causes הכשר: makes food able to become טמא
You shall pour it out like water

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching explains why רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement fits blood. The blood of קרבנות has a source showing it does not cause הכשר. Water has no such source.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
From where do we know that blood of consecrated offerings does not make food susceptible to impurity?
As it is said: 'You shall pour it on the ground like water,'
blood that is poured out like water makes food susceptible,
phrases.notes: The opposite case (blood not poured like water does not) continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the scriptural basis for the answer in step 26 that blood of קדשים is the exception.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'liquids' in רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement are blood, because blood of קדשים does not cause הכשר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן (quoted by רבי חייא בר אבא) learning from 'על הארץ תשפכנו כמים' (דברים יב:טז).
